argument_summary: The admissible record does not support a clean certification finding. It does support a narrower position: certification is policy-consistent only as caveated compliance, because the known student-aid weakness is expressly disclosed and the mitigation record is completed to the policy-required standard before launch. Aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents support launch readiness in general, and public monitoring guidance supports managing residual risk, but those points do not erase the current disclosure obligation for a known limitation.
claims_about_business_cost: No independent business-cost claim is needed to resolve the audit issue. The narrower caveated-compliance treatment preserves the locked certification direction while keeping the record aligned to the stated policy requirements.
claims_about_policy: The governing policy standard in the record is specific: certification without material caveats requires either no current material weakness or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. The admissible evidence shows the student-aid issue remains below target and the current runbook is still draft with required fields marked TBD, so a clean certification predicate is not satisfied. The supportable policy reading is therefore caveated compliance: certify only with the student-aid limitation disclosed in the model card and with the mitigation record completed to policy standard before launch.
concessions: The current record does not support a clean no-caveat certification position.
Public risk-management guidance cannot substitute for the case-specific approval elements the policy requires.
The draft mitigation artifact, as described, is not yet an approved mitigation.
Aggregate readiness evidence alone is insufficient to overcome a known material limitation in a named launch use case.
